newsitem.title: USA: IVAX sees Q3 loss, restructuring charges.
newsitem.headline: IVAX sees Q3 loss, restructuring charges.

text.p: IVAX Corp said on Monday it expects to post a third quarter operating loss of $35 million, not including a $13 million pre-tax restructuring charge.
IVAX said the restructurings are aimed to save the company $20 million a year before taxes.
IVAX said it expects to close its Shreveport, Louisiana, plant by the end of 1996 and its Syosset, New York, facility by the end of the first quarter in 1997.
Production at these facilities will be transferred to a Kirkland, Canada, plant the company is expected to acquire from Glaxo Wellcome Plc, IVAX said.
Distribution at its Northvale, New Jersey, and Mason, Ohio, facilities will be consolidated to a site in Kentucky that is being built, IVAX said.
Administrative functions at the Fort Lauderdale facility will be moved to Miami late in 1996 or early 1997, IVAX said.
IVAX said the third quarter will be hurt by high inventory levels, lower prices for generic drugs, and higher reserves for returns and inventory write-offs.
In addition, a leading customer who owed IVAX $16 million filed Chapter 11 during the third quarter, leading the company to add to its reserves for uncollectable accounts, the company said.
As a result of the loss, IVAX said it expects to be out of compliance with the provisions of its revolving line of credit. The company said it is presently negotiating with lenders.
